py-eval.message: `eval(user_input)` executes arbitrary code. Use a safe parsing approach (e.g. `json`, `ast.literal_eval`) with validation.

py-secret.message: A live API key is hardcoded in source. Move it to environment variables/secret management and rotate the exposed key.

py-shell.message: `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True)` from untrusted input enables shell injection; pass an argument list and avoid `shell=True`.

py-bare-except.message: Bare `except:` swallows all exceptions, including `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit`. Catch specific exceptions, or at least `except Exception`, and log/re-raise.

py-http-timeout.message: `requests.get` is called without a timeout, so a hung server can block this call indefinitely. Pass an explicit `timeout`.

py-pickle.message: Deserializing untrusted data with `pickle.loads` allows arbitrary code execution. If `raw` can come from an external/untrusted source, use a safe format (e.g. JSON) instead.

py-yaml.message: `yaml.load(text)` without `SafeLoader` can execute arbitrary code on untrusted input. Use `yaml.safe_load(text)`.

py-eval-shell.message: `eval(raw)` on untrusted input is arbitrary code execution. Replace with a safe parser or an explicit allow-list of operations.
`subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True)` from unsanitized input enables shell injection. Pass an argument list without `shell=True`.

py-pickle-yaml.message: `pickle.loads` on untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution; prefer a safe serialization format such as JSON.
`yaml.load(text)` without `SafeLoader` can instantiate arbitrary Python objects and execute code. Use `yaml.safe_load(text)` or pass `Loader=yaml.SafeLoader`.

ts-dangerous-html.message: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` renders raw HTML directly, which enables XSS if `html` contains user-controlled content. Sanitize the HTML (e.g. DOMPurify) before injecting, or render as text.

ts-innerhtml.message: Assigning to `innerHTML` executes embedded scripts/markup and allows XSS when `v` comes from user input. Use `el.textContent = v` or sanitize the HTML first.

ts-eval.message: `eval()` on arbitrary input is a code-injection vulnerability and is prohibited. Remove eval and use a safe, explicit parser/whitelist of allowed operations.

ts-token.message: Hardcoded GitHub personal access token committed to source. Secrets must not be stored in the codebase — remove it and load from environment/config at build or runtime, and rotate the leaked token.

ts-two-xss.message: Unsanitized `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` allows XSS. Sanitize `html` before rendering or use normal React children (auto-escaped).
Directly inserting `userInput` via `innerHTML` is an XSS vulnerability. Use `node.textContent = userInput` or sanitize before insertion.

java-exec.message: Public method passing an externally supplied `cmd` to Runtime.exec — command injection risk. Restrict to a fixed command whitelist or avoid shell execution; also note exec() does not split arguments.

evidence.existing_code: public void run(String cmd) throws Exception { Runtime.getRuntime().exec(cmd); }

java-sql.message: SQL injection: `id` is concatenated directly into the query. Use a PreparedStatement with a bind parameter instead of string concatenation.

evidence.existing_code: void find(Statement stmt, String id) throws Exception { stmt.executeQuery("select * from t where id=" + id); }

java-password.message: Hardcoded production credential in source. This is a critical security issue; load it from a secret manager/env var and remove it from the repository.

java-printstack.message: `e` is not declared in this scope (no try/catch or parameter), so this won't compile. Additionally, printStackTrace() without a logger loses the stack trace context in production; use a logger and propagate/handle the exception properly.

java-exec-password.message: Command execution with an unvalidated parameter — a command-injection sink. Also, the added lines are inserted before the existing `public class Danger {` declaration, so there are now two class declarations and the enclosing brace structure is broken (won't compile).

evidence.existing_code: void a(String cmd) throws Exception { Runtime.getRuntime().exec(cmd); }

java-exec-password.message: Hardcoded secret literal in source; move to external secret configuration and rotate the exposed value.

Duplicate `public class Danger {` declaration (line 1 and line 3) makes the file uncompilable. In addition, the class is missing a closing brace, so even after removing the duplicate declaration the structure is broken. Also, the `void a(String cmd)` method is package-private dead code that is never called — either remove it or make it a legitimate, validated API.

py-eval-timeout.message: `eval(raw)` on untrusted input is arbitrary code execution; use a safe parser instead.
`requests.get` is called without a timeout; a slow server can block indefinitely. Pass an explicit `timeout`.
